transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for coming in today. I asked to meet with you because I have some information regarding your grandson's developmental screening. There has been a mistake in how his referral was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean? I thought everything was being taken care of.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be very clear about what happened. When you declined that first appointment for the screening, someone in our office marked the referral as completed in the computer system. Because it was marked as finished, no one ever reached out to you again to reschedule it. This means the screening didn't actually happen. Does that make sense, or can I explain that differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand why it would be marked as finished if he never went. I just thought maybe the timing wasn't right and God would provide a better moment for it. But to think he was just... forgotten?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. Our team failed to follow up with you, and that is our responsibility. We missed this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It feels so cold. You all have your screens and your charts and you just click a button and a child's needs just vanish. I've been praying for his progress, and all this time I thought we were just waiting on the Lord's timing, but it was just a button?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you feel let down and perhaps a bit heartbroken that this happened while you were trusting the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am heartbroken. I just want what is best for him. I can't believe this is how the clinic works.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is distressing. I want to make sure I’ve explained the a—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did it happen? Was it just one person? Was anyone watching the files?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are currently investigating the exact sequence of events to see why the system allowed that mark to be made without a confirmation. I don't have the final answer on the "how" yet, but the fact is that the error occurred and he didn't get the screening. Does that answer your question about the current status?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose. It just feels so clinical. I feel like I'm talking to a wall sometimes in this building. I just want to know that you actually care about the boy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do care about him and I care about your family. I feel terrible that we missed this opportunity to support his development.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? I can't just leave here today not knowing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We need to get him in for that screening as soon as possible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Next month?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to look into the scheduling. We'll see what we can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an answer. I need a date. I need to know he's being seen.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a date this second, but I'll get back to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're doing it again. Just giving me a vague answer. I feel like I'm chasing you for information.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I have to go see another patient now, but I will keep an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? Now? While I'm sitting here upset?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just mean we can wrap this up for now and I'll check the calendar.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just so dismissive. I feel like my faith and my worries are just a nuisance to your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize for the mistake with the referral, and I really do want to fix it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fix it how?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned for an email or a call from the office. Someone will reach out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if they don't?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, they should. Just wait for the call.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have to go see another patient now', 'wrap this up') and shows defensive escalation under pushback.

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense...', 'Does that answer your question...').

A.justification: Direct apologies used ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and responsibility explicitly accepted ('that is our responsibility', 'We missed this').

R.justification: Specific emotions named back ('let down', 'heartbroken') and references the patient's trust and faith.

T.justification: No concrete plan provided; resident uses placeholders ('look into the scheduling', 'stay tuned', 'wait for the call').
